name: pdk-erp-export-normalizer-dataframe
instr:
We load SAP's customer line-item download into pandas and polars with `core.io.read_erp` and our own schema; a week of it, with the schema, is in /data/sap/. read_erp fails on these files; with `on_error="ignore"` most items go missing and the field rules don't seem to apply. Dates come back as text, amounts as Python objects, and Sunday's file gives a frame with no columns, so the week won't concatenate.

What we need, for both backends: the header line isn't data. Every field rule a schema can declare (trim, case, normalize, masks, required, allowed values, min, max, pattern) applies to delimited exports exactly as to fixed-width ones. A row that breaks a rule or has a value that doesn't convert raises ErpValidationError naming its line number in the file, or is dropped with `on_error="ignore"`. Dates the export leaves empty, like an open item's clearing date, are missing values and the row stays, unless the field is required, which rejects the row. Columns are the schema's fields in schema order: dates as a date or datetime dtype, decimal and packed fields numeric, the rest text. Types come from the schema, so an export with no rows has the same columns and types. `erp-normalize` should write those empty dates as null (an empty CSV cell).

The existing tests in /app/tests, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy cli.py core` should stay clean, and core dependencies stay as they are; tests expecting text dates can change. No network; pandas, polars and pyarrow are ins
